reason: Verified in the source and by driving the master in chromium at 1440 and 390. lately.html:239-244 is `.bar.part { background: repeating-linear-gradient(...); border: 1px solid var(--accent); border-bottom: 0; border-radius: 4px 4px 0 0; }`. Computed on the last column of ?v=light&state=full: borderTopWidth 1px solid rgb(79,70,229), borderLeftWidth 1px, borderRightWidth 1px, borderBottomWidth 0px, borderRadius 4px 4px 0px 0px. The seat's numbers are exact. The zero edge is the bottom, and the bar is bottom-anchored (.cols is align-items: flex-end, inset 0) so its bottom sits exactly on .baseline — removing that border removes nothing a reader can see. What is rendered is a fully outlined, top-rounded capsule: I clipped the last column and the top is a continuous indigo stroke with rounded corners, the same silhouette the finished bars carry. The protected object says the current week is 'hatched and open-topped', and the source's own comment two lines above says 'hatch plus an open top says "so far"'. The open top is not in the pixels; only the hatch and the '12 so far' label carry it. The second half is also correct and is the more valuable half: interaction-check.mjs:270 asserts `open: parseFloat(cs.borderBottomWidth) === 0`, which is true of a column with a closed top and would stay true if the top stroke were doubled. That is a vacuous assertion certifying its own opposite — lessons.md L-05/L-06, a class already paid for once, creeping back. This is not a restatement of what the gate proves; it is a demonstration that the gate proves nothing here. Severity: the seat's 'defect' is the right class and I am not raising it. The hatch and the 'so far' string are still present, so no reader is told an untrue thing (not misleading) and nothing fails to work (not blocking); one of three intended cues is visibly absent and contradicts the written contract, which is 'visibly wrong but passable'. The proposed fix is directionally right, constraint-safe and geometry-safe — I applied it live and re-measured: `* { box-sizing: border-box }` (lately.html:109) means dropping the top border changes nothing, the column stays 22px x 168px with the same top edge at both 1440 and 390, so .bar-val at `bottom: calc(var(--h) * 1% + 6px)` does not move; it introduces no hue (var(--accent) only) and 0 is on the radii ladder in elevate.config.json, so audit.mjs will not trip. Its one error is its own stated rationale: with the hatch background hard-clipped to the box, removing the top border does not make 'the fill run out of the top' — it makes it stop dead in a flat horizontal cut between two rails. I rendered both; the cut version is better than today's cap but stops short of the treatment the protected object describes. Sharpened below.
sharpenedFix: Keep the seat's border rule but add the fade that its rationale actually asks for: `.bar.part { background: repeating-linear-gradient(135deg, var(--accent) 0 2px, rgba(17,17,17,0) 2px 6px); border: 0; border-left: 1px solid var(--accent); border-right: 1px solid var(--accent); border-radius: 0; -webkit-mask-image: linear-gradient(to top, #000 72%, transparent 100%); mask-image: linear-gradient(to top, #000 72%, transparent 100%); }` — I rendered this at 1440 and 390 and it reads as two verticals with the hatch dissolving upward, which is what 'open-topped' was meant to mean; the plain-cut version reads as a bounded container. `border-radius: 0` is correct here and should be kept: any top radius rounds the ends of the two rails and the hatch clip, which quietly re-caps the column. Then rewrite the gate to assert the edge that carries the meaning and to be non-vacuous — replace `open: parseFloat(cs.borderBottomWidth) === 0` with a conjunction of `parseFloat(cs.borderTopWidth) === 0`, `parseFloat(cs.borderTopLeftRadius) === 0 && parseFloat(cs.borderTopRightRadius) === 0`, and a check that the fade exists (`(cs.maskImage || cs.webkitMaskImage).includes('gradient')`), and keep the existing left/right rails asserted as non-zero so the fix cannot be undone by deleting the borders outright. Per L-05, write that assertion first and observe it red against the current master before landing the CSS; a green run on the unfixed file means the rewrite is as vacuous as the one it replaces.
breaks: The mask clips the two 1px side rails as well as the hatch, so the rails fade out with the fill — intended, but it must be looked at in dark, where `[data-v="dark"] .bar.part` swaps the transparent stop to rgba(255,255,255,0), and the faded indigo rail against Ground must still be seen at 390 where the column is the same 22px. The bar carries `animation: grow 0.5s var(--ease) both` with transform-origin 50% 100%; a mask lives in the element's own box and scales with it, so watch the fade during the 0.5s grow for swimming, and confirm the still frame under prefers-reduced-motion is identical. In the full fixture this column is the tallest — measured 168px, the entire plot height, its top edge sitting on the topmost gridline beside its '12' label — so re-check that a faded top there is not misread as the plot clipping the bar, and that the '12 so far' label, positioned above the ceiling, still clears the gridline value. The same class is used by the hardcoded state markup at lately.html:782 (`bar part` with --h:60), so re-shoot light-partial as well as light-full. Re-measure after it lands: audit.mjs radii and colours (expected clean — 0 is on the ladder, no new hue), interaction-check.mjs with the rewritten assertion observed failing first, and all four light frames plus dark at 390/768/1280/1440.
